body.p: The Final Office Action of September 1, 2023 (Office Action) has been carefully reviewed. The Applicant respectfully requests the Examiner to reconsider the rejections and allow the pending claims in view of the following remarks.
Claims 1-2, 5-6, and 9-34 stand rejected.
Claims 2, 20, and 30 are canceled.
Claims 1, 5, 10, 15, 17, 19, 21, 25-27, 29, 31, and 32 are hereby amended.
New claims 35-37 are added herein.
Thus, claims 1, 5-6, and 9-19, 21-29, and 31-37 remain pending in this application.

p.u: REQUEST UNDER AFTER FINAL CONSIDERATION PILOT PROGRAM 2.0

body.p: Applicant respectfully requests that the claim amendments be entered pursuant to the AFCP 2.0 because those amendments place the Application in condition for allowance by adding new limitation(s) while only requiring a limited amount of further consideration/search by the Examiner. Applicant further notes an AFCP request form (i.e., Form PTO/SB/434) is filed herewith, and respectfully requests an interview with the Examiner if entry of the amendments is deemed inappropriate under AFCP 2.0.
Claim 5 is objected to due to informalities. See Office Action, p. 2. Specifically, the Final Office Action states that claim 5 should be amended to read "wherein the rigid object comprises..."

See id. By this response, claim 5 has been amended based on the Examiner's suggestion in the Office Action. For at least this reason, the Applicant requests that the objection to claim 5 be withdrawn.

Claims 1-2, 5-6, 9-11, 15-21, 25-26, and 28-34 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2019/0133689 to Johnson, et al. ("Johnson") in view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2019/0262084 to Roh, et al. ("Roh").
Claims 12-14 and 22-24 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Johnson in view of Roh and U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2018/0078439 to Cagle, et al. ("Cagle").
Claim 27 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Johnson in view of Roh and U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2017/0296277 to Hourtash, et al. ("Hourtash")

Claims 2, 20, and 30 are cancelled. Claims 5-6, 9-18, and 32-34 depend from independent claim 1, claims 21-24 depend from independent claim 19, claims 26-28 depend from independent claim 25, and claim 31 depends from independent claim 29. Therefore, claims 1, 5-6, and 9-19, 21- 29, and 31-34 will be allowable over the cited art when independent claims 1, 19, 25, and 29 are allowable over the combination of Johnson and Roh. The United States Supreme Court in Graham v. John Deere Co. of Kansas City noted that an obviousness determination begins with a finding that "the prior art as a whole in one form or another contains all" of the elements of the claimed invention. See Graham v. John Deere Co. of Kansas City, 383 U.S. 1, 22 (U.S. 1966). The Applicant respectfully asserts that the cited prior art fails to disclose all of the limitations set forth in independent claims 1, 19, 25, and 29, and consequently does not render obvious claims 1, 5-6, and 9-19, 21-29, and 31-34.
Independent claim 1 as amended recites:
1. A robotic medical system, comprising:
a platform;
one or more robotic arms coupled to the platform;
a console configured to receive input commanding motion ofthe one or more
robotic arms;
a processor; and
at least one computer-readable memory in communication with the processor
and having stored thereon a model of the one or more robotic arms and
computer-executable instructions to cause the processor to:
control movement of the one or more robotic arms in a workspace based on the input received by the console,
receive an indication of a plurality of objects being within reach of the one or more robotic arms, wherein the objects comprise a rigid object and
a non-rigid object,

update the model to include a representation of the objects in the workspace, wherein the representation of the rigid object is based on a pre- modeled representation stored on the computer-readable memory, and wherein the representation of the non-rigid object comprises one or more zones corresponding to the non-rigid object within the workspace based on a
user input received at the console,
detect a collision between the one or more robotic arms and at least one of the objects, and
in response to the collision being detected, update the model based on the collision to include an updated representation of the at least
one of the objects.
(Emphasis added). As shown above, independent claim 1 as amended recites a robotic medical
system configured to detect a collision between the one or more robotic arms and at least one of the
objects, and in response to the collision being detected, update the model based on the collision to
include an updated representation of the at least one of the objects. Independent claims 19 and 29
recite similar features.
The Office Action has not asserted any prior art for the foregoing features of independent
claims 1, 19, and 29, particularly to the features of updating a model of the robotic arms based on a
detected collision between a robotic arm and an object in response to detecting the collision between
the robotic arm and the object.

Nevertheless, the Applicant submits that neither Johnson nor Roh, either alone or in combination, teaches a robotic medical system configured to detect a collision between the one or more robotic arms and at least one of the objects, and in response to the collision being detected, update the model based on the collision to include an updated representation of the at least one of the objects, as recited by independent claims 1, 19, and 29. Moreover, the Applicant submits that Cagle and Hourtash, either alone or in combination, also fail to disclose or render obvious the foregoing features of independent claims 1, 19, and 29.

Therefore, the cited prior art fails to disclose all of the limitations set forth in independent claims 1, 19, 25, and 29, and consequently does not render obvious claims 1, 5-6, and 9-19, 21-24, 29, and 31-34.
Next, independent claim 25 as amended recites: 25. A robotic medical system, comprising:
a platform;
one or more robotic arms coupled to the platform;
a console configured to receive user input;
a processor; and
at least one computer-readable memory in communication with the processor
and having stored thereon a model of the one or more robotic arms and the platform
and computer-executable instructions to cause the processor to:
receive an indication of one or more keep-out zones based on the user input received at the console, wherein the user input indicates a region of the
model,
update the model to include the one or more keep-out zones, detect a collision between the one or more robotic arms and an object, and
in response to the collision being detected, update the one or more keep-out zones based on the collision.

(Emphasis added). As shown above, independent claim 25 recites a robotic medical system configured to detect a collision between the one or more robotic arms and an object, and in response to the collision being detected, update the one or more keep-out zones based on the collision.

Again, the Office Action has not asserted any prior art for the foregoing features of independent claim 25, particularly to the features of updating a model of the robotic arms and the keep out zones based on a detected collision between a robotic arm and an object in response to detecting the collision between the robotic arm and the object.

Nevertheless, the Applicant submits that neither Johnson nor Roh, either alone or in combination, teaches a robotic medical system configured to detect a collision between the one or more robotic arms and an object, and in response to the collision being detected, update the one or more keep-out zones based on the collision, as recited by independent claim 25. Moreover, the Applicant submits that Cagle and Hourtash, either alone or in combination, also fail to disclose or render obvious the foregoing features of independent claim 25.
Therefore, the cited prior art fails to disclose all of the limitations set forth in independent claim 25, and consequently does not render obvious claims 25-28.

New claims 35-37 recite novel and non-obvious aspects of the disclosure. Support for new claims 35-37 is found in paragraphs 156-157 of the application. Thus, no new matter is contained in these claims. New claims 35-36 depend from claim 1, and new claim 37 depends from claim 29, both ofwhich are allowable for the reasons stated above. Thus, new claims 35-37 are also allowable.

Consideration of the foregoing amendments and remarks, reconsideration of the application, and withdrawal of the rejections and objections is respectfully requested by the Applicant. No new matter is introduced by way of the amendment. It is believed that each ground of rejection raised in the Final Office Action dated September 1, 2023 has been fully addressed.
